sharedRules.name: Bazooka Skirts
sharedRules.description: A Tank Team with Bazooka Skirts increases its Side armour to 5 against weapons with Firepower 5+ or 6.

sharedRules.name: Flame-thrower
sharedRules.description:
Infantry, Gun, and Unarmoured Tank Teams re-roll successful Saves when hit by a Flame-thrower and the Unit is automatically Pinned Down. Armoured Tank Teams use their Top armour for Armour Saves when hit by a Flame-thrower.

Flame-throwers my shoot in Defensive Fire. However, while a Unit that is Hit by a Flame-thrower is Pinned Down, this does not automatically stop the assault. The defender still needs to score five (or eight) hits as normal to stop the assault.

sharedRules.name: HEAT
sharedRules.description: A Team's Armour rating is not increased by +1 if it is more than 16"/40cm away when hit by HEAT weapons.

sharedRules.name: Limited #
sharedRules.description:
Each time this Unit shoots, # number of its Teams may shoot as that Weapon rather than its usual weapons.
Each time this Unit rolls To Hit in an Assault, # number of its Teams may attack with that Weapon rather than its usual weapons.

sharedRules.name: Mounted Assault
sharedRules.description: This Team has improved Assualt and Counterattack with one Passenger and in some units has a further improved Assault with two or three Passengers. This is shown on the Transport Unit card as an additional motivation and skill column.

sharedRules.name: Old Hand
sharedRules.description:
An Old Hand Formation Commander gives Units from their Formation whose Unit Leader is within 6"/15cm of the Formation Commander an improved Tactics Raiting.
Units from a Heavy Tank Training Company or Tank Training Company improve their Tactics rating to 4+.
Units from a Berlin Battle Group improve their Tactics rating of 3+ if worse, otherwise it has no effect.

sharedRules.name: Salvo
sharedRules.description:
Weapons with a ROF of 'SALVO' are Artillery weapons and fire Artillery Bombardments, but use a 10"/25cm square Salvo Template rather than the normal 6"/15cm square Artillery Template.

A Salvo Template may not be placed within 6"/15cm of a friendly Team.

sharedRules.name: Stormtroopers
sharedRules.description: The Unit may attempt a second Movement Order after succeeding in its first Movement Order. The second Movement Order must be different from the first.

sharedRules.name: Unit Transport
sharedRules.description: The Unit Leader of the Transport Attachment must end the Movement Step within 6"/15cm of the Unit Leader of its Passenger Unit while on the table. If it cannot do this, then the Transport Attachment must be Sent to the Rear.

sharedRules.name: Bombs
sharedRules.description: Bombs do not need to re-roll successful rolls To Hit for only having 1 or 2 weapons firing. Only Teams from the Bombarding Unit can Spot for it.

sharedRules.name: Self-Defense AA
sharedRules.description: Self-Defense weapons can Shoot at Aircraft with ROF 1.

sharedRules.name: Dedicated AA
sharedRules.description: Dedicated AA weapons can Shoot at Aircraft using thier Halted ROF.

sharedRules.name: Gun Shield
sharedRules.description: A Gun Team with a Gun Shield is in Bulletproof Cover when Shot at from in front of the Team's base. A Gun Shield does not offer any protection against Artillery Bombardments or if the Team moved at Dash speed.

sharedRules.name: Large Gun
sharedRules.description: Large Guns cannot be placed in buildings and cannot be placed from Ambush (page 103) within 16"/40cm of enemy Teams.

sharedRules.name: Unarmoured
sharedRules.description: An Unarmoured Tank team cannot Charge into Contact and must Break Off if assaulted.

sharedRules.name: Assault #
sharedRules.description: Teams with the Assault # special rule use the # number ofor To Hit rolls in Assaults rather than the normal one shown on the card.

sharedRules.name: Guns
sharedRules.description: Gun Teams have a worse Assault rating.

sharedRules.name: Heavy Weapon
sharedRules.description: A Heavy Weapon Team cannot Charge into Contact, but may be an Assaulting Team if in Contact with an enemy Team. Heavy Weapons have a worse Assault rating.

sharedRules.name: Overworked
sharedRules.description: Overworked weapons add +1 to the score needed To Hit when moving.

sharedRules.name: Passengers #
sharedRules.description: A Transport Team can carry Infantry Teams as Passengers. The # indicates how many Teams can be carried.

sharedRules.name: Protected Ammo
sharedRules.description: Tanks with Protected Ammo have a better Remount rating.

sharedRules.name: SP Gun
sharedRules.description: SP Guns have a worse Counterattack rating and a worse Assault rating. If they are Open-topped, they have a significantly worse Counterattack rating.

sharedRules.name: Tractor
sharedRules.description: A Tractor Team can tow a single Gun Team as a Passenger. The gun model is placed behind the Tractor to show that it is being towed.

sharedRules.name: Brutal
sharedRules.description: Infantry, Gun, and Unarmoured Tank Teams (including when Passengers) re-roll successful Saves against Brutal Weapons.

sharedRules.name: Forward Firing
sharedRules.description: Forward-firing weapons can only target Teams fully in front of the shooting Team, and can only fire an Artillery Bombardment if the Aiming Point is fully in front of the shooting Team.

sharedRules.name: No HE
sharedRules.description: A weapon with No HE targeting an Infantry or Gun Team, adds +1 to the score needed To Hit.

sharedRules.name: Overhead Fire
sharedRules.description: Grenade launchers and light mortars capable of Overhead Fire can fire over friendly teams.

sharedRules.name: Pinned ROF #
sharedRules.description: These weapons have a ROF of # when Pinned Down.

sharedRules.name: Slow Firing
sharedRules.description: Slow-Firing weapons add +1 to the score needed To Hit when moving.

sharedRules.name: Smoke
sharedRules.description: Smoke weapons can Shoot Smoke ammunition (page 65).

sharedRules.name: Smoke Bombardment
sharedRules.description: Smoke Bombardment weapons can fire a Smoke Bombardment once per game (page 71).

sharedRules.name: Observer
sharedRules.description: An Observer Team can Spot for any friendly Artillery Unit (page 66).

sharedRules.name: Scout
sharedRules.description:
Scouts are Gone to Ground unless they Shoot or Assault. This means that if they are Concealed, the enemy will suffer an additional +1 penalty to hit them (page 56). 

Scouts have a worse Last Stand rating. Open or Wheeled Scout tanks also have a significantly worse Counterattack rating and a worse Assault rating as well.

sharedRules.name: Spearhead
sharedRules.description:
When a Spearhead Unit is placed on table during Deployment (but not if it arrives from Reserves or is placed outside the normal Deployment Area using this rule), the player may immediately Move its Teams at Tactical or Dash speed.

This movement may not use any Movement Orders, and may not take a Team within:
	- 16"/40cm of an enemy Team it is not Concealed from, 
	- 8"/20cm of any enemy Team,
	- 16"/40cm of the enemy Deployment Area or any Objective outside your own Deployment Area.

When Deploying their remaining Units, a player may treat the area entirely within 8"/20cm of a Spearhead Team that is In Command as an extension of their Deployment Area. Teams placedhere may not be placed in the areas that a Spearhead Team may not move into.

sharedRules.name: Independent
sharedRules.description: Unit cannot Charge into Contact or take an Objective, and is ignored for Victory Points.

sharedRules.name: Recoilless
sharedRules.description: The Team cannot be Concealed if the Recoilless weapon shot in the previous Shooting Step.

sharedRules.name: Local Militia
sharedRules.description: Volkssturm and Hitlerjugend Platoons always begin the game on the table. Volkssturm and Hitlerjugend Platoons in your Force count as being worth 0 points when calculating Reserves.

sharedRules.name: Tank Escorts
sharedRules.description: Tank Escort teams can Shoot while Mounted on Armoured Tank Teams (to a maximum of one StG44 assault rifle team shooting per Tank), and can Dismount when Charging into Contact.

sharedRules.name: Infra-Red (IR)
sharedRules.description: A Unit with Infra-Red rolls two dice on the Night Visibility Table and chooses the highest score.

sharedRules.name: IR Searchlight
sharedRules.description: A Unit with an Infra-Red (IR) Searchlight may, instead of Shooting, Illuminate a target in Line of Sight within 32"/80cm. To do this the Unit with the Infra-Red special rule does not need to roll for Night Visibility and can automatically see out to 32"/80cm. All Units with the Infra-Red (IR) special rule may Shoot at that target without rolling for Night Visibility. Hits may be allocated to Teams from the same Unit within 6"/15cm of the target Team.

sharedRules.name: Night Fighters
sharedRules.description:
If a Force with Night Fighters is the Attacker in a mission without the Meeting Engagement rule, the player may attack at night. If they do so, Night Fighting Dawn rules (page 109) are in effect at the start of the game. 
Units from Formations with Night Fighters can move freely from the start of the game. Other Units from other Formations or Support in the Force, unless equipped with Infra-Red (IR), may not move out of their Deployment Area while the game is played in Darkness, but can move when Dawn breaks.

sharedRules.name: Uhu
sharedRules.description:
An Sd Kfz 251 Uhu Tank Team is sent to the rear at the beginning of their first Movement Step in which the game is fought in Daylight. An Sd Kfz 251 Uhu removed in this fashion does not count as Destroyed, and if Bailed Out, automatically Remounts.
An Sd Kfz 251 Uhu Tank Team is brought forward at the beginning of their first Movement Step in which the game is fought at Night. Before moving an Infra-Red (IR) equipped Unit, you may place its Sd Kfz 251 Uhu on the table.
The Sd Kfz 251 Uhu must be placed within 4"/10cm of a Team from the Unit, and may not be:
- within 16"/40cm of any enemy Team within Line of Sight, unless Concealed by Terrain from it, or
- within 4"/10cm of any enemy Team.

Once Brought Forward in this way, the Sd Kfz 251 Uhu must move at Dash Speed (and therefore cannot shoot or Assault this turn), but may Illuminate a target with its Infra-Red (IR) Searchlight.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: While the Panzer divisions have individual trucks for each Panzergrenadier section and a car for the platoon leader, Panzergrenadier divisions have fewer bigger trucks with the leader riding with the troops.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
This Infantry or Gun Unit may add a Softskin Transport Attachment. The number of vehicles in the Unit is as follows:
•	Add one Softskin Transport for every two Infantry Teams in the Unit.
•	Add one Softskin Transport for each Gun Team in the Unit.
The characteristics of an Softskin Transport are shown on the back of this card.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text: Discard this card to re-roll any one die. The second result must be used.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
If the Unit Leader did not Move, discard this card to pick an enemy Infantry or Gun Team in Bulletproof Cover up to 12"/30cm away from, and in Line of Sight of, the Unit Leader. Roll a Skill test for the Unit Leader instead of Shooting:
- If passed, the enemy Team is Hit with a Firepower 3+ weapon and their Unit is Pinned Down. Infantry and Gun Teams must re-roll successful saves.
If the line between the Unit Leader and the enemy Team crosses Terrain mor than 2"/5cm from the enemy Team, roll a die for each item of terrain. Any roll that is not 4+ causes the attack to miss. If the line crosses any Impassible Terrain, the attack misses.

characteristics.$text: Sd Kfz 251 half-tracks in the third platoon of the Panzerpionierkompanie are fittedwith Wurfrahmen, frames for six huge 28cm rockets. These were so devastating that they were called Stuka zu Fuss - Stuka on foot.

Weapon: 28cm rocket

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: German infantry dug camouflaged nests for their heavy machine-guns, covering them with soil mounted over doors and beams stolen from wrcked houses.

characteristics.name: Details
characteristics.$text:
sMG34 or sMG42 HMG teams in this Unit cannot Move, but can rotate to face the target when Shooting, and are Nests.
Each HMG team is a separate Independent Team.
Nest: The Nests are always Concealed and in Bulletproof Cover.
Teams attacking a Nest must re-roll successful Firepower tests to Destroy it.
Nests cannot Charge into Contact.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: Two turret designs were used on the Tiger II. The initial design is sometimes called the 'Porsche' turret due to the belief that Porsche designed it for their prototype. This turret is in face the initial Krupp design for both prototypes. These early models also had less armour and a number of mechanical issues.

Panzerdivision in France, and leading Panzer Regiment Coburg in the east, earning a Knight's Cross. Now he leads Panzer Regiment Muncheberg defending the eastern approaches to Berlin.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The final organisations of the heavy armoured car company of the Panzeraufklarungsabteilung (armoured reconnaissance battalion) had four platoons, each broken into three troops of two Sd Kfz 234, consisting of once Sd Kfz 234/1 (2cm) and either a Sd Kfz 234/3 (7.5cm) or a Sd Kfz 234/4 (7.5cm PaK40) for heavy fire support.

characteristics.name: Info
characteristics.$text: The 10.5cm leFH 18/40 howitzer is the lightened version of the standard German field howitzer. It uses the light carriage of the 7.5cm PaK40 anti-tank gun, as well as wheels of lighter contruction, but with a bigger muzzle brake to reduce recoil. The new design saves materials for the war effort and makes it easier to manhandle for its crews.

The brigade was commanded by SS-Obersturmbannfuhrer Hans Stern and fielded two regiments. The unit was a motley collection of training and convalescent forces supported by heavy armour and various infantry formations.

They are normally kept behind the German front line, but as the Soviets rapidly advance they keep finding themselves in the thick of the battle. Heavy AA guns like the 10.5cm FlaK39 were soon proving themselves capable anti-tank weapons.
